name: CROSS
full_name: Cryogenic Rare-event Observatory with Surface Sensitivity
summary: CROSS is a cryogenic double-beta-decay demonstrator at Canfranc. Its programme develops low-background bolometers, surface-event rejection and sensitive light detection for molybdenum-100 and related rare-decay searches.
detection_principle: Cryogenic absorbers measure deposited energy, with scintillation-light signals and surface-sensitive response used to distinguish alpha and surface backgrounds. Fast light sensors also reduce accidental coincidence backgrounds.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
